exposure: prenatal period overlap with the COVID-19 PHE
outcome: hybrid prenatal care vs. in-person-only prenatal care
cohort: The study analyzed electronic health record data from 349,682 nationwide pregnancies among 349,524 people who gave birth from June 1, 2018, through May 31, 2022, across 75 health systems in all 50 US states.
finding: During the COVID-19 PHE, hybrid prenatal care increased substantially, but pregnant people in rural areas had lower levels of hybrid care, while individuals belonging to racial and ethnic minority groups (Hispanic/Latino, non-Hispanic Asian, non-Hispanic Black) were more likely to receive hybrid care than non-Hispanic White people.
